boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named IU Bloomington spaces where students can study, collaborate, find support, make projects, or pause between classes, verified through current university sources.

cards.title: Head Up the East Tower for Quiet Work
cards.subtitle: Quiet study above a collaborative main floor
cards.notes: Use the East Tower’s upper floors for quiet individual work, or book a Scholars’ Commons room on the main floor for collaboration.
cards.short_summary: One building offers both quiet stacks and reservable group space.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries identifies Wells Library as a student research hub and says the East Tower’s upper floors offer quiet study, while its main floor has reservable Scholars’ Commons rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located at 1320 E. Tenth Street. Consult the library’s live hours display before visiting; reservable rooms may require IU credentials.

cards.title: Build a Group Session Around a Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: Collaborative work on Wells Library’s first floor
cards.notes: Bring a small team to a first-come collaboration room, then use the nearby technology and research support to move the assignment forward.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich workspace designed for assignments from start to finish.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries describes the Learning Commons as a collaborative, technology-infused learning center with first-come rooms for four to six people, workstations, and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Wells Library West Tower, first floor. IU login credentials are required for student workstations; check the live hours display before arrival.

cards.title: Switch Between Quiet and Group Study
cards.subtitle: Two study modes inside the Wright Education Building
cards.notes: Choose a quiet seat for reading or reserve an enclosed room when your project needs conversation without disturbing individual study.
cards.short_summary: A compact branch library with separate options for solo and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries says the Education Library combines quiet study areas with reservable enclosed group-study spaces and serves students, faculty, and staff affiliated with the School of Education.
cards.access_notes: Room 1160 on the first floor of the Wendell Wright Education Building. Rose Avenue and Seventh Street entrances have ADA push buttons.

cards.title: Claim a Small Collaboration Room
cards.subtitle: Group work where SPEA meets Hodge Hall
cards.notes: Reserve one of the small collaboration rooms for a focused team session, with workstations, printing, and scanning close at hand.
cards.short_summary: A discipline-focused library equipped for small-team projects.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Libraries states that the Business/SPEA Library has 14 collaboration rooms for groups of one to six, plus 44 workstations, three printers, and a scanner.
cards.access_notes: SPEA room PV 150 at 1315 E. Tenth Street, where the O’Neill SPEA building meets Kelley’s Hodge Hall. Rooms are reservable for up to two hours.

cards.title: Match the Room to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Quiet desks, group rooms, and gathering areas at La Casa
cards.notes: Try the computer room for quiet classwork, the conference room for a group project, or a gathering area when the work is more social.
cards.short_summary: A cultural center with several clearly documented ways to study and connect.
cards.evidence_claim: La Casa documents computers for students, comfortable gathering rooms for study and group projects, and a conference room, computer room, library, and sunroom used for classwork.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year hours listed by La Casa are 9 a.m.–9 p.m. Monday–Thursday and 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Friday; summer and finals-week schedules differ.

cards.title: Do Homework in an Affirming Gathering Space
cards.subtitle: Resources, community, and a place to settle in
cards.notes: Stop in to work, browse the LGBTQ+ library, or ask staff about campus resources; use the accessible rear ramp if needed.
cards.short_summary: A student support center that explicitly welcomes homework and informal connection.
cards.evidence_claim: The IU LGBTQ+ Culture Center says it is an inclusive gathering space and specifically invites students to hang out, do homework, meet people, and use its LGBTQ+ library.
cards.source_title: We welcome you!: LGBTQ+ Culture Center
cards.access_notes: Located at 705 E. Seventh Street. The center lists Monday–Friday hours of 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; the first floor is accessible via a rear ramp.

cards.title: Connect at the Native Student Gathering Place
cards.subtitle: A central hub for Native experience at IU
cards.notes: Visit for connection, cultural programming, or student support, and approach the center as a community space with a specific mission.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated gathering place supporting Native and Indigenous students.
cards.evidence_claim: IU describes the First Nations Educational & Cultural Center as a gathering place and central hub for Native American students, offering support, resources, and cultural activities.
cards.source_title: About: First Nations Educational & Cultural Center
cards.access_notes: This is a mission-specific community and support space. Review the center’s current contact and program information before planning a visit.

cards.title: Pause Quietly Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Individual reflection inside the Indiana Memorial Union
cards.notes: Use this quiet room for individual prayer, reflection, or a brief reset, and preserve the calm, inclusive purpose of the space.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet room for personal spiritual or reflective needs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Indiana Memorial Union describes its Interfaith Prayer and Reflection Space as a quiet, inclusive area where individuals can address personal or spiritual needs.
cards.access_notes: Located in the K.P. Williams Room on the IMU’s second floor. The official page lists the space as open daily from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.

cards.title: Give a Student Organization Somewhere to Work
cards.subtitle: Gathering and collaboration space in the IMU
cards.notes: Bring organization planning to the center’s gathering space, or ask support staff how to connect a project with IU student involvement resources.
cards.short_summary: An IMU base for student groups, collaboration, and involvement support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Indiana Memorial Union identifies the Student Involvement and Leadership Center as the home of student-organization gathering and collaboration space, IU Student Government, and support staff.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the Indiana Memorial Union. Organization spaces and staff services may follow their own schedules or eligibility rules.

cards.title: Work With Scores and Music Technology Nearby
cards.subtitle: A research environment built around music study
cards.notes: Set up a music-focused research session near the collections, then use the library computers or printers when notation and page size matter.
cards.short_summary: A specialized study environment connecting music research, technology, and performance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cook Music Library says it supports musical performance, teaching, learning, and research, while its technology page documents public-area wireless access, computers, and three printers.
cards.source_title: Mission and Vision of the Cook Music Library
cards.access_notes: Street address is 200 S. Eagleson Avenue. General research is open to students, faculty, staff, and the public, but special collections have registration rules.
